subject: Request: CAPEX-friendly sizing + GPU price-sensitivity guardrails for Horizon deal
content:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@horizonlabs.ai>, procurement@horizonlabs.ai
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: CAPEX-friendly sizing + GPU price-sensitivity guardrails for Horizon deal

Alex / Horizon procurement team —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, Horizon is asking for a reserved/dedicated capacity proposal that balances near-term cost predictability with some protection against GPU market volatility. I attached a quick sizing worksheet (horizon_sizing_options_v2.xlsx) and a one-page term summary (term_summary_draft.pdf) that sketch three options:

- Option A: 6-month ramp, 50% baseline reserve, burst pool. Lower initial commit, higher price-per-token.
- Option B: 12-month committed pool with tiered discount based on absolute GPU-hours. Middle ground for cost and predictability.
- Option C: 24-month firm commit with a price-floor clause and quarterly usage true-ups — best unit economics but higher up-front exposure.

We're flagging two asks for our side so procurement can consider:
1) A pricing guardrail tied to an agreed GPU price index (monthly look-back) that allows a modest unit-price step if market GPU costs move >15% quarter-over-quarter.
2) A fallback SLA/ops play: if reserved capacity utilization exceeds X% and we need to reallocate across regions, we'd want an agreed burst entitlement and a short notice change window.

Sean and Marissa — can you review the attached scenarios and confirm what discount ladder we can offer under Option B (12 months) with a conservative GPU-price contingency? Ideally we want a pre-approved executive band so we can give Horizon a quick answer.

Alex — can you confirm expected average QPS and peak window (tokens/min) so the sizing sheet's traffic profile aligns with your forecast? Also, procurement, any timing constraints for a PO or SOW to hit before your quarter close?

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0198
Attachment: horizon_sizing_options_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: term_summary_draft.pdf (pdf)

-----Original Message-----
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@horizonlabs.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizonlabs.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:08:12 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: CAPEX-friendly sizing + GPU price-sensitivity guardrails for Horizon deal

Hi Tessa —

Appreciate the clear options. Quick answers from our side:
- Average QPS (inference) over the next 12 months: 350 qps (model mix: 60% small gen, 30% embeddings, 10% large gen bursts).
- Peak windows: up to ~1,200 qps for 30-45 minutes during product events (we can share historical traces).
- Procurement timeline: we need signed terms and a PO by Sept 2 to make this quarter's budget.

Two asks back:
1) Can Redwood include a mid-term re-evaluation clause at 6 months to re-size without penalty if our traffic stays materially below forecast?
2) Can we get a limit on upward price adjustments tied to the GPU index (cap of +10% per quarter on price increases)?

I'll upload our usage trace to the shared link after this message.

—Alex
VP of Engineering, Horizon Labs

On Mon, 17 Aug 2026 at 11:02 Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Alex — noted on the PO date. Sean, Marissa — the timeline is tight; Horizon needs a signable term set by Sept 2. Can we propose a conditional approval path where we commit to Option B pricing subject to finance exec sign-off and a short call with Horizon procurement?
>
> I propose we host a 30-min call on Wed to walk through the index mechanics. I can run the product/ops side and Sean can speak to pricing bands. Marissa — would you be comfortable committing to a preliminary discount ladder for the call?
>
> Tessa
>

> Team — quick pricing scenarios (Option B focus):
>
> Scenario 1 (Conservative): 12-mo commit, baseline 250 GPUs equivalent (Horizon forecast normalized), Discount ladder: 8% at MSR (minimum spend range), + additional 3% if they hit +20% monthly utilization for 3 consecutive months. GPU-index contingency: allow +12% unit price if GPU index increases >20% q/q; no unilateral decreases below floor.
>
> Scenario 2 (Aggressive): 12-mo commit, baseline 200 GPUs eq., Discount ladder: 12% at MSR, +5% at higher tranches; GPU-index contingency capped at +8% per quarter with a maximum +18% annual adjustment. Requires finance approval for exposure >$1.2M.
>
> Notes: We can table Option C (24-mo firm commit) for a separate exec pitch — finance likely wants deeper safeguards for multi-year exposure.
>
> Marissa / Neha: can you confirm which scenario you can greenlight up to $1.2M without needing CFO or CEO sign-off? Also operationally, we should confirm burst bandwidth entitlements (region fallbacks) in the term sheet.
>
> -Sean
>Principal, Sales Operations
>
> -----
> On Mon, 17 Aug 2026 at 12:22 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
> To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
> Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@horizonlabs.ai>, procurement@horizonlabs.ai
> Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 12:22:09 -0700
> Subject: Re: Request: CAPEX-friendly sizing + GPU price-sensitivity guardrails for Horizon deal
>
> Team / Alex —
>
> I reviewed the scenarios. Finance is comfortable with Scenario 2 as a negotiable baseline under these conditions:
>
> 1) Horizon signs a 12-month SOW within 2 weeks (by Aug 31) and commits to a minimum monthly spend floor equal to 60% of the baseline.
> 2) Any GPU-index-based upward adjustment will be applied only if external GPU cost reports (industry index we agree on) confirm a sustained move and we limit adjustments to a cumulative +15% over the 12-month term.
> 3) Redwood retains right to propose a quarterly usage true-up; material downward true-ups (>25% below baseline) trigger a re-sizing discussion but not automatic rebates.
>
> For exposure: I can approve up to $1.2M in discounted revenue within my sign-off authority. Anything beyond that requires CFO review. If Horizon needs the +10% cap Alex requested, we can offer that as a negotiated exception but it drops the available discount lane by ~3 percentage points.
>
> Alex — if you can confirm the PO timing and the minimum monthly spend comfort, we can lock Scenario 2 as the working term for the Sept 2 deadline and route for CFO sign-off if we exceed the $1.2M threshold.
>
> Best,
>
> Marissa Cole
> Director, Revenue Finance, Redwood Inference
>Attachment: finance_exposure_note_v1.pdf (internal)
